Subject: Processing locality & subprocessor coverage — Aurora Health

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our internal procurement and security review I need a concise explanation of where Aurora customer inference requests are executed and which third parties are involved. Specifically we need answers to: 

- Which cloud regions or physical sites can handle our inference requests by default (hosted + dedicated)?
- Do requests ever transit outside the US for hosted customers in the US region? If so, under what circumstances?
- Full list of subprocessors involved in the inference path (runtime, logging, monitoring, key management), and whether any of them can access raw request payloads.
- KMS arrangement: do you use a customer-managed key option? If we provide a CMK, is data encrypted at rest and in transit with that key in all paths?
- Deletion/erasure: when a user requests deletion, what steps are taken (caches, KV, backups), and typical time-to-complete for complete removal?

If you have a short evidence packet (diagram + inventory) we can attach to our vendor assessment. Appreciate a reply by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Best,
Claire
Security & Procurement — Aurora Health

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Jordan and Monica are copied for technical and retention specifics respectively. Attaching our current subprocessor inventory and a regional execution map.

- Regions/sites: For hosted customers you can select US (us-east-1) or EU (eu-west-1) control plane and execution zoning. By default US-hosted inference runs on capacity in our US regions (primary: us-east NVidia farms, fallback: us-west). Dedicated deployments are pinned to the customer’s reserved pool/region.

- Cross-border transit: For US-hosted customers we do not intentionally route inference payloads to outside the US. Exceptions: (1) transient egress to a global CDN endpoint for static assets (not raw payloads), (2) automatic fallback to a warm pool in another region if there is a localized outage and the customer has accepted failover in their config. All such cross-region fallbacks are logged and can be disabled on the account level.

- Subprocessors: Runtime (Redwood runtime), GPU cloud infra (third-party cloud provider), observability backend (metrics/logs vendor), KMS provider (cloud KMS or optional HSM). See attached inventory for names and contract status. None of our observability partners receive long-term raw request payloads — we redact payloads before logs persist.

- KMS/CMK: We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key via supported cloud KMS). If you supply a CMK we can bind model cache encryption at rest and key-wrapping for persistence snapshots. In-transit TLS with mutual auth is enforced across the service mesh.

- Deletion: High-level process: 1) API tombstone request -> 2) purge active KV/prefix caches -> 3) remove persisted artifacts (snapshots, logs) subject to retention SLAs -> 4) kick-off background re-encode to propagate deletes to backups and analytics stores. Typical completion window for primary runtime data: 24–72 hours; full propagation to backups/analytics can take up to 30 days depending on retention and legal hold. Monica will confirm SLA windows.

I’ve attached: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_v2.pdf and regional_processing_map_v3.png.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

> Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our internal procurement and security review I need a concise explanation of where Aurora customer inference requests are executed and which third parties are involved. Specifically we need answers to:

> - Which cloud regions or physical sites can handle our inference requests by default (hosted + dedicated)?

Hi Claire — adding technical details to Markus’ summary: 

- Routing policy: Requests are evaluated by policy at the edge. For US accounts the edge returns endpoints in US regions unless the account is explicitly configured for multi-region. Policy keys: account_region_tag, latency_threshold, and fallback_tier.

- KV/Cache behaviour: We keep per-account prefix caches in memory on serving nodes; those are ephemeral and cleared immediately on a tombstone request. Long-lived persisted caches (to speed up cold starts) are encrypted at rest and have TTLs managed by the account’s config.

- Observability: Traces and aggregated metrics stream to our telemetry partner. Raw request bodies are not stored in traces. If a customer opts into advanced logging for debugging, payloads are redacted at collection time and stored under a short retention window configurable per account.

- KMS specifics: CMK flow: customer grants Redwood a crypto-operations-only grant (no plaintext export). We perform wrapping and unwrapping using the CMK; master keys never leave the customer’s KMS. For on-prem/private deployments we support HSMs reachable via VPN.

- Failover example: In a regional outage we may promote a warm pool in another US region (us-west) — this is not an international failover unless the account explicitly opted into global failover.

Happy to share a short network diagram if that’s helpful.

—Jordan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Claire — quick note on deletion/retention SLA windows to supplement Markus’ earlier message.

- Primary runtime data: tombstone -> cleared from runtime nodes within minutes; fully purged from active infrastructure within 24–72 hours depending on model cache size.
- Logs and observability: default retention 30 days; sensitive payloads are redacted on ingestion. We can provide a shorter retention window for Aurora under contract.
- Backups/analytics: backups are rotated; full removal from long-term backup media depends on rotation schedules and can be up to 30 days; we support escrow/accelerated purge as a professional service for urgent erasure requests.

Evidence we can provide: audit logs showing tombstone request IDs, a scoped sample of subprocessor contracts (redacted), and a signed technical attestation of data flow. Let me know what evidence bundle you need and we’ll prepare it.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
